where: blaze: the watches outside every view on Linux (blaze-vfs outside, blaze-usercode inputs)
what: The no-op lane never answered on Linux. Four causes found with a serde fixture on blaze-vm and an event that says, for each path a walk looked at, who looked and the watch's generations: a watch's wake that names no file (Linux marks the whole file system, so every write wakes every watch) was taken as a change; a cover kept with an answer stayed on a directory whose watch a directory above had taken over; `Files::entry` looked every time; a traced name's whole directory was asked of, so `/root/wt` made `/root` (the daemon's home under it) never quiet.
cost: every build with nothing changed walked: 3 s on reth, 3.1 s on a serde fixture (78 ms after the first three fixes)
cause: the watch table was only ever exercised where the watch is per directory and quiet (macOS FSEvents on a dev machine)
whys: why a walk: the lane refuses
why: the walk looked at a path
why: on Linux every watch hears every write and an empty wake counted as a change; a name was vouched for by its whole directory tree
property: semantics tested on one platform's event shape and one directory layout
class: a platform's event shape assumed (rule simulate-first: the simulation never delivered an empty wake or noise beside a name)
prevention: built (lane reth-1112, merged by noopkeep): empty wake is no change; a cover follows its taker; names are asked of by name (`Dirs::watch_name`); a walk's file looks are kept and looked at again; each with an invariant and a control in outside/tests.rs and noop/tests.rs. Not built: the simulated driver delivering empty wakes and file-system-wide noise by default
fix: 5c53498.., 45d5677.., ab8b2fb416, efaf95ca43 on reth-1112; in int-good 7b970bbe0d
state: fixed on a fixture (walk 78 ms; the lane's answer on Linux not yet measured on the merged tree)
